newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ housing confidence rebounds - ASB survey.
newsitem.headline: NZ housing confidence rebounds - ASB survey.

text.p: Confidence in the New Zealand housing market rebounded in the three months to October, ASB Bank said on Monday.

The latest ASB Bank Quarterly Housing Survey showed a net 16 percent of respondents in the October quarter believed it was a good time to buy a home, more than double the net seven percent in the three months to July.

Auckland showed one of the biggest rises in confidence, with a net 12 percent believing it was a good time to buy, compared to the April quarter survey where a net 11 percent felt it was a bad time to buy.
Wellingtonians were the most optimistic of all, with a net 16 percent of respondents believing it was a good time to buy, against 11 percent in Christchurch.

ASB said expectations of a rise in house prices seemed to be the driving reason behind the positive outlook of Wellington residents. Of the Wellingtonians who felt it was a good time to buy a house, 54 percent cited this as the main reason for their confidence.
Nationwide, a net 34 percent expected house prices to rise over the next 12 months, up from 28 percent.

Interest rate expectations improved significantly throughout the country. A net 19 percent of respondents expect a rise in interest rates over the next year, compared to a net 56 percent in the previous quarter.
Aucklanders were the least pessimistic about interest rates, with a net 14 percent expecting a rise, against 27 percent in Wellington and 18 percent in Christchurch.
ASB said the outlook for 1997 was mixed.
"Given the recent pick-up in consumer confidence and reductions in interest rates, the outlook for real estate activity is positive," ASB said.
"However, as we have seen over recent years, affordability could once again be eroded if lower interest rates place fresh upward pressure on house prices."
